title: Avoiding Reverse Falls in Drainage Piping
description: One of the most common and damaging installation mistakes in drainage piping is the creation of a reverse fall or 'belly.' When a pipe lacks consistent downward slope toward the main sewer, wastewater slows down and solids begin to settle out of the liquid. Over time, this accumulation leads to recurring clogs, pipe corrosion, and potential structural backups. Professional installers always verify grade continuously using proper measuring tools rather than relying on visual estimation alone. Ensuring a uniform pitch protects the entire drainage system and prevents premature failure.

Professional installers always verify grade continuously using proper measuring tools rather than relying on visual estimation alone. Ensuring a uniform pitch protects the entire drainage system and prevents premature failure.
